newsitem.title: ITALY: Initial deal struck on Italian bank restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Initial deal struck on Italian bank restructuring.

text.p: Italian banking association ABI and union leaders reached a preliminary agreement with the centre-left government late Wednesday over job cuts in the banking sector, the prime minister's office said in a statement.

The deal gives unions and management 60 days to finalise plans for a comprehensive overhaul of working practises in the sector, which analysts say is heavily overstaffed by comparison with banks in other European countries.
The accord, reached after 10 hours of talks between the various parties, foresees the creation of a national fund which is expected to help finance eventual lay-offs in the sector.
Banks will be asked to give the fund a sum equivalent to 0.5 percent of their total salary bill.
Unions and management also signalled the need for greater flexibility over contracts and schemes to help workers directly invest in their banks.

Cabinet undersecretary Enrico Micheli and Labour Minister Tiziano Treu mediated Wednesday's marathon negotiating session. Unions and management will now work together on the fine print with the government pledging to review the situation in a month.

Banking analysts have warned that overstaffing must be addressed rapidly and radical restructuring implemented if the Italian banking sector is to achieve the sort of profitability seen elsewhere in Europe.
